label: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
output:
Here's a draft — plain prose so you can paste it straight in:

---

4 stars, and I'd book them again without much hesitation.

Moved at the end of October, Phibsborough up to Drumcondra. Two-bed flat, but mostly my stuff rather than both of ours, and a 4th floor walk-up at the new place — so the kind of move where everything goes up four flights no matter how good the van is.

I booked through the website, €50 deposit by Revolut, quote of €340 for up to 4 hours with two lads and the van. The job took about three and a half. The two other quotes I got were €450 and up for the same thing, so on price alone they were well clear of everyone else, and I did compare properly before I called anyone.

The bit they lost a star for: timing. We were meant to start at 9 and they turned up at half 10. I got a text at 8:40 saying the previous job had overrun, which is a real reason and I believe it, but it was still an hour and a half of me sitting on boxes with a coffee going cold. Not the end of the world for me because I wasn't working to a landlord deadline, but if you've got a handover slot or a key handover you're depending on, build in a buffer. They can and do run late.

What I appreciated was that Dessie knocked €40 off afterwards and I never even had to ask. He didn't argue it or make it a thing, he just did it, and that told me more than anything else here. No awkwardness about it either.

The thing that actually annoyed me was the lamp. They chipped the base of a brass floor lamp — my nan's lamp, and yeah, I care about that more than I'd like to say. They wrapped everything else in blankets and did that well, but the lamp base got knocked and there's a chip in the brass now. It's only a lamp, but it was mine and I was a bit gutted about it. So genuinely, if you take one thing from this: wrap your own lamps. Blanket, box, bit of tape round the base, five minutes of work and you save the headache. That's the only damage on the whole move, but it's the only bit I'd think twice about.

There's a lot of good stuff too. The couch wouldn't go round the turn on the third floor — everyone knows the type, the hallway one that catches you out every time. One of the lads (Kev, I think) took the legs off it with an Allen key he already had in his pocket and it went straight up the stairs after that. No "that's an extra", no phoning the boss about it, just sorted it on the spot. That's the sort of thing you remember.

They put the bed back together for me after and I never asked them to. They also took the flat-pack shelf away that I didn't want, which I hadn't even mentioned — they spotted it and asked. Small stuff, but it's the difference between a crew doing a job and a crew actually turning up in your place and treating it like a move instead of a van hire.

So yeah: late, chipped my lamp, and I still reckon they were the right call, because the alternative was paying over €100 more and hoping for better. If you're moving a normal-sized flat in Dublin and you want to spend the money on the right job rather than the cheapest quote, they're well worth a look.

Just wrap the lamps.
